meta.summary: Base case keeps Costco's growth runway intact but normalizes segment margins modestly from FY2026 highs so the terminal operating margin sits inside, rather than at the top of, the 10-year history. The model still shows a large valuation gap versus the share price, so the stance remains valuation-sensitive rather than operationally bearish.

Segment sales per warehouse is computed from 10-K segment sales and total warehouse count because regional historical warehouse counts were not provided for all three years.

notes.growth: Base case is consensus-like: total FY2027/FY2028 growth is driven by roughly 2.7% annual warehouse growth plus mid-single-digit sales-per-warehouse growth, fading as the base scales. FY2026 release: total adjusted comparable sales +6.6%, U.S. +6.6%, Canada +6.7%, Other International +6.5%; 10-K Item 1: warehouses rose from 890 to 914 to 939 and Nov. 10, 2026 8-K: 945 warehouses.
notes.margin: Base margins no longer fade below the recent uptrend. The FY2026 documents show Costco's scale model, negative working-capital retail economics, $5.907bn of membership fees, rising paid members and private-label mix support, while also noting wage investment and low-price reinvestment; the base therefore holds modest operating leverage rather than assuming continued margin fade. The bull margin path is not the base case; it is a reverse-DCF calibration so the scenario range includes the share price, with consolidated terminal margin approaching the model's price-required margin.

w_pg.note: Primary method for a high-ROIC, going-concern membership retailer; cash-flow duration and terminal reinvestment are the key questions.

w_exit.note: Secondary DCF cross-check using a market multiple implied by the forecast economics; no manual exit multiple is set.

w_sotp.note: Costco is one integrated warehouse-club model; geographic segments share buying, membership, supply-chain and corporate infrastructure, so a breakup SOTP is not a realistic value anchor.

w_comps.note: Comps are useful for market context but peer differences are material: Walmart includes Sam's plus general merchandise / grocery, BJ is smaller and U.S.-only, Target and Kroger lack Costco's membership economics.

peer_discount.note: No arbitrary quality premium or discount; Costco's quality should be captured by growth, margins, ROIC and the regression / own-band comps framework.

exit_pe.note: Near the current P/E on FY2026 adjusted EPS (53.3x)

other_stake.note: Equity stakes / investments not captured in segment EBITDA (none material on the balance sheet)

fade_years.note: 2032E growth remains above the 3.75% house terminal growth rate because warehouse expansion and membership productivity still have runway; growth fades over five years rather than forcing terminal growth higher.

comps_pe_weight.note: Large-cap retail and membership models are primarily assessed on EPS/P-E; EV/EBITDA is retained as a secondary check because lease/capex intensity and net cash differ by peer.

ronic.note: Set to roughly FY2032E ROIC including goodwill, consistent with gate 34 and the PM review; Costco's goodwill/intangibles are immaterial in the supplied data, so there is no acquired-growth reason to haircut terminal new-capital returns.

thesis.recommendation: The setup is valuation-sensitive because Costco's defensive quality and long runway are already capitalized at a reverse-DCF IRR of {irr} versus {wacc}.
points: 1. Growth: the base case follows an operating path driven by warehouse-count growth plus comparable-sales productivity, with growth fading toward mid-single digits by FY2032.

2. Margin: base margins no longer fade below the recent uptrend; the model assumes Costco retains some scale, membership-fee and private-label benefit while still reinvesting in price, wages and member value.

3. Capital return: the Nov. 10, 2026 $30 special dividend and approximately $13.3bn cash outflow are modeled in FY2027, with regular dividend growth resuming thereafter and repurchases paced to cash generation and authorizations.
4. Quality: membership renewal remains the moat, with FY2026 92.3% U.S./Canada renewal, 89.8% worldwide renewal and Executive members representing about 75.2% of worldwide net sales.
model_says: • Fair value {fv} is triangulated from {dcf_pg}, {dcf_exit} and {comps}; the bear and bull cases are {bear} and {bull}.
• The reverse-DCF IRR at the current price is {irr} versus WACC of {wacc}, and the 3-year model return is {ret3y}.
• The bull case is calibrated to the reverse-DCF requirement: either a materially higher terminal margin near {req_margin} or a much longer growth runway near {req_g} would be needed.
risks: • Bull risk: renewal rates remain near FY2026 levels, international unit economics scale faster than modeled, and membership / private-label mix lifts margins without sacrificing traffic.

• Bear risk: wage inflation, shrink, fuel / FX mix, or tariff reinvestment pressure pushes the U.S. segment margin toward the low-3% bear path while sales growth slows one historical sigma below base.
• Multiple risk: Costco's premium P/E can persist longer than a DCF-driven analyst expects, especially if defensive compounders remain scarce.
• Capital allocation risk: future special dividends are discretionary; holding too much cash would dilute returns, while debt-funded returns would change the risk profile.
monitor: • December 2026 / Q1 FY2027 sales release and earnings: adjusted comparable sales versus the FY2026 +6.6% baseline and traffic / ticket mix.
• Warehouse count: pace from 939 at FY2026 year-end to 945 on Nov. 10, 2026 and the FY2027 net-opening cadence.
• Membership metrics in the next 10-Q / 10-K: paid-member growth, Executive penetration and U.S./Canada renewal rate versus 92.3%.
• Margin: merchandise-cost ratio and SG&A leverage after the FY2026 wage increase and tariff-refund reinvestment.
thesis.about: Costco Wholesale operates a global membership warehouse-club model with 939 warehouses at FY2026 year-end and 945 reported on Nov. 10, 2026.
thesis.price_implies: At the current share price, the reverse DCF produces {irr} long-run IRR; closing the valuation gap would require a combination of longer above-GDP growth duration and terminal margin materially above the base case.
thesis.variant_view: We differ from a simple premium-quality narrative by assuming Costco reinvests most scale and membership benefits into price and wages; this is tested by FY2027 quarterly operating margin and adjusted comparable-sales cadence, beginning with Q1 FY2027.
catalysts: Q1 FY2027 earnings: test whether operating margin stays near the FY2026 run-rate while adjusted comparable sales remain mid-single-digit or better.
Monthly sales releases through spring 2027: watch total and ex-gas/FX comparable sales against the FY2026 +6.6% benchmark.
FY2027 capital allocation updates: confirm the $30 special dividend cash outflow and pace of repurchases under the $4bn authorization.
thesis.breaker: The valuation concern breaks if Costco can compound sales per warehouse above 5% beyond FY2028 while expanding consolidated operating margin sustainably above the high end of its 10-year range without a traffic slowdown.
thesis.sensitivities: The two largest sensitivities are terminal operating margin / RONIC and the duration of above-GDP warehouse-plus-productivity growth; buyback pace is secondary because the stock trades at a high multiple.
thesis.consensus_notes: Costco did not provide FY2027 guidance in the materials entered here. If the model differs from consensus by more than 3%, the variance should come from explicit operating drivers: normalized segment margins, lower interest income after the special dividend, and no assumption of future discretionary special dividends.

explanations.gate 5: Peer EPS inputs have been reset to each peer's company guidance available before Nov. 13, 2026 rather than the post-date Nov. 16 consensus snapshot; Dollar General and Dollar Tree are excluded because dollar-store traffic, basket and margin economics are not close enough to Costco's warehouse membership model.
explanations.gate 10: Post-balance-sheet 8-Ks reviewed: Oct. 14, 2026 announced a $1.47 quarterly dividend; Nov. 10, 2026 announced a $30 special dividend, about $13.3bn total payment, and a $4bn repurchase authorization. No acquisition, divestiture, debt issuance, impairment or ASR settlement was disclosed.
explanations.gate 16: Terminal margin has been brought back inside the historical range by fading base segment margins modestly from FY2026 levels rather than underwriting continued expansion to a new high.
explanations.peer p e outliers vs the 17 4x: Walmart remains in comps because Sam's Club and Walmart grocery are direct competitors named in Costco's 10-K Item 1; it is an outlier multiple, so comps receive only 20% weight and the peer set excludes less comparable dollar stores.
explanations.cash builds to 75 417mm 43 of total: Stale prior cash-build warning: after modeling the Nov. 10, 2026 $30 special dividend, the $4bn repurchase authorization and later excess-cash repurchases, FY2032E ending cash in the current model is $27.2bn, about 6.2% of FY2032E net sales, not $75.4bn or 43% of sales.
explanations.fair value is 51 vs the price before: Stale prior warning key retained only to explain the old check. The current base still indicates a large valuation gap, but the model has now corrected RONIC to ROIC including goodwill, removed the unsupported base-margin fade, and rebuilt the bull case from the reverse DCF instead of using the gap as a standalone call.
explanations.fair value is 55 vs the price before: Stale prior warning key retained only to explain the old check. The current base still indicates a large valuation gap, but the model has now corrected RONIC to ROIC including goodwill, removed the unsupported base-margin fade, and rebuilt the bull case from the reverse DCF instead of using the gap as a standalone call.
explanations.gate 34: Fixed by setting valuation.ronic to 32.0%, approximately the model's FY2032E ROIC including goodwill. The prior 25.0% assumption was an unexplained haircut; the supplied documents do not show a dated competitive step-down, loss of exclusivity, or recurring acquisition program that would justify new capital earning materially less than the return including goodwill.
explanations.gate 41: Fixed by recalibrating the bull case from the reverse DCF. The bull scenario now approaches the model's price-required terminal margin near {req_margin}; this is not the base case, but it makes the scenario range encompass the current share price as required.
explanations.fair value is -54% vs the price: The base-case valuation remains well below the current share price even after fixing RONIC and removing the prior margin fade. That gap is treated as a valuation-risk observation rather than a standalone short thesis: Costco's supplied operating data support a high-quality compounder, but the reverse DCF still shows only {irr} at the current price versus {wacc}.
explanations.pm review:
Recommendation rule: changed thesis.stance from short to neutral, rewrote thesis.recommendation as one supporting sentence without a call or bias, and added rating_override to explain why the valuation rule is overridden. Value effect: no direct model-value effect; it changes the investment stance to reflect the absence of short evidence.

Bear-bull calibration: rebuilt the bull case from the reverse DCF by ramping bull segment margins toward the model's price-required terminal margin near {req_margin}. Value effect: raises the bull case so the current price sits inside the bear-bull range; it does not change the base case except through the separately stated base-margin correction.

RONIC: changed valuation.ronic from 25.0% to 32.0%, matching the model's ROIC including goodwill and the PM instruction that goodwill is negligible. Value effect: raises DCF value by reducing terminal reinvestment required for the same terminal growth.

Short requirements: removed the outright short framing. No dated premium-compression episode, borrow/crowding check, or pair-trade support was supplied in the source documents; the setup is therefore treated as a valuation-risk case rather than a short.

Claims/data discipline: adjusted_eps is set to null because the supplied Costco release reports GAAP EPS, not company non-GAAP adjusted EPS. The supplied 8-Ks after the balance sheet show dividends, a special dividend, repurchase authorization and warehouse count updates, but no deal, debt issuance or impairment.

Cyclical normalization: Costco is modeled as a defensive compounder, not a cyclical, but the margin normalization issue was addressed symmetrically by removing the unsupported fade below the recent uptrend rather than forcing a trough-like terminal margin.

Deals: no announced acquisition, separation or signed pending deal appears in the supplied post-balance-sheet 8-Ks, so deals remains empty and no synergy credit is modeled.

Peer EPS: the current peer set does not show a next-year EPS decline worse than 20% in the entered data, so no peer was excluded on the one-off EPS rule in this pass.

Cost of debt: the supplied documents do not include an agency rating. The kd note was rewritten so it is an estimate and not a synthetic-AAA agency-rating claim; the value was not moved without a sourced rating.

COST-specific stance: re-rated via rating_override because the useful output is the reverse-DCF IRR of {irr} versus the risk-free rate and WACC, not a short catalyst. The PM-cited decade P/E range was not entered as a sourced data claim because it was not in the supplied documents.

RONIC for COST: fixed to 32.0% as above, consistent with ROIC including goodwill.

Margins for COST: base segment margins now hold a modest uptrend instead of fading below the recent level, reflecting the supplied evidence on scale, renewal, paid-member growth, private-label support and membership fees, offset by reinvestment in wages and member value.

Membership fee cycle: the supplied documents disclose the current $65 U.S. annual fee, paid members, renewal rates and membership-fee revenue, but they do not provide the prior fee-increase date or a 5-6 year cadence. I therefore did not add a discrete 2030 fee step as a sourced event; instead the base margin path includes modest membership economics support, and the absence of a sourced fee-cycle schedule remains a monitoring item.

Reverse-DCF bull: bull margins were recalibrated to the model's price-required terminal margin so the current price is inside the scenario range.

rating_override.reason: The model's valuation gap alone is not enough for a Short: no dated premium-compression catalyst, borrow/crowding evidence or pair-trade evidence was supplied, and the business is a low-volatility compounder.

flags: Costco did not provide FY2027 sales, margin, EPS or FCF guidance in the supplied September 24, 2026 FY2026 earnings release; FY1 is anchored to operating KPIs and analyst assumptions, not company guidance.
Costco does not report company-adjusted EPS in the supplied documents; adjusted_eps fields are set to null and the model should not treat GAAP EPS as company non-GAAP EPS.
FY2026 included a $0.15 diluted EPS non-recurring IEEPA tariff-refund benefit disclosed in the September 24, 2026 release; it is not forecast as run-rate.
No agency-rating source was supplied for the valuation-date cost of debt; kd is left as an estimate and the note no longer claims a synthetic agency rating.
The bull case is a reverse-DCF calibration rather than the base underwriting case; it is included to make the scenario range encompass the current share price.
